name: Bank of Georgia headquarters
elevationDatum: Rigid local foundation y=0; real metres +X east, +Y up, +Z south. Two mapped controls fix rotation, baked into the geometry once. No terrain or Mercator stretch.
note: Five two-storey concrete office bars interlock at right angles above three circulation cores, with real cantilevered ends, open gaps, two recessed ribbon-window rows and gridded soffits. No reliable surveyed height was located: 51 m is explicitly an estimate from 17 OSM levels at 3 m, while published descriptions call the tallest core 18 storeys. Bar elevations follow OSM level/min-level ratios, not a terrain survey. The third core, within the left-hand bar and lower crossbar intersection, is estimated from the photographs; its 6 × 7 m plan is an authoring approximation. All three foundations use one rigid y=0 datum; the steep hillside and actual footing elevations require later Full 3D world fitting. The detached modern glass entrance cube, landscaping and access ramps are outside this asset. Photo 4 shows the different old city-centre bank and is excluded. Cityscape: not tested; Full 3D world: not tested.
